title: Tolerant field-level adapter and canary schema rollout for usage ingestion
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a tolerant, field-level adapter in the usage event ingestion pipeline that can heal minor schema drift at runtime and enable progressive, per-tenant canary rollouts of new schemas. The goal is to reduce ingestion failures from schema mismatches while preserving strict validation for critical fields and keeping downstream analytics correct.
acceptance_criteria: New adapter introduced as a pluggable stage in the ingestion pipeline that runs before canonical validation
Adapter can apply a configurable per-field transformation (coerce, default, rename) based on tenant rules
Canary rollout mechanism to enable adapter rules for a subset of tenants with metrics and rollback
Ingestion error rate for schema-related failures reduced by >60% for enabled tenants in canary
All changes are covered by unit + integration tests and a QA run on staging with synthetic drift cases
tasks: Design adapter API and config format (per-tenant, per-route)
Implement adapter stage in ingestion consumer (Go service)
Add rule engine: actions = [coerce_type, set_default, rename_field, drop_field]
Integrate canary flag evaluation using existing tenant routing middleware
Expose metrics: drift_count, healed_count, drop_count, validation_failure_count
Create rollout playbook and Grafana dashboards/alerts
End-to-end tests with synthetic drift scenarios
Performance benchmark to ensure <5% added p50 latency at 99th percentile load
comments: 2025-11-10 - Aisha Patel: Spiked a prototype that applies simple coerces and defaults. Initial perf impact negligible on low QPS.
2025-11-12 - Jordan Kim: Reviewed prototype. Need to formalize config schema and ensure no silent data loss; add auditing for dropped/renamed fields.
2025-11-13 - Marco Li: Recommends conservative defaults: run adapter only in 'heal' mode when validation would otherwise error. Also add telemetry tags for rule provenance.
2025-11-15 - SRE (via comment): Concern about cardinality growth from per-tenant rules in metrics. Suggest aggregate metrics and sample-based tracing.
2025-11-17 - Jordan Kim: Implemented initial rule engine and canary flag toggle; created PR and staging deployment for QA. Added unit tests for coercion and rename rules.
2025-11-18 - QA: Staging run with 5 synthetic drift scenarios. Adapter healed 4/5 cases; one case requires schema migration (complex nested arrays) and should go to PM for contract change.
2025-11-18 - PM (Elena Morris): Agreed to coordinate contract change for nested array case. We will start a separate migration plan and keep adapter limited to flat-field tolerances.
2025-11-18 - Jordan Kim: Next steps: add audit log to S3 for all healed events, finalize dashboard panels, and schedule a small canary with two internal tenants next week.
notes: Trade-offs: Allowing automatic heals reduces immediate errors but can mask upstream producers with buggy instrumentation. To mitigate, every heal emits an audit event and increments healed_count.
Security: No PII transformation will be performed by the adapter. Any rule that touches PII must be reviewed and approved by Security (flagged in UI).
Observability: Use sampled event traces to surface original vs healed payload in internal viewer; limit to 1% sampling to control costs.
Rollback plan: Toggle canary off; run a backfill job to reingest healed events without adapter if needed. Keep backups of raw envelopes for 30 days.
owner_notes: Plan to pair with Product for clear communication to customers. Begin canary with internal tenants to validate non-customer facing instrumentation before broader rollout.
